sections.html:
Barnstable is the county seat of Barnstable County and the largest community on Cape Cod by land area and population, roughly 70 miles southeast of Boston. Cape Cod Bay forms its northern edge and Nantucket Sound its southern edge.

The town is a group of villages with no legal boundaries of their own. These seven are the ones most often listed:

  • Barnstable village, which includes Cummaquid
  • Centerville
  • Cotuit
  • Hyannis, which includes Hyannis Port and West Hyannisport
  • Marstons Mills
  • Osterville
  • West Barnstable

Most residents live in the south, many near the beaches of Centerville and Hyannis Harbors. Hyannis, the biggest village, is the commercial center of the Cape, with Cape Cod Hospital, Barnstable Municipal Airport and the ferries to Nantucket and Martha's Vineyard. Route 6 runs across town as a four lane freeway, and the nearest year-round commuter rail is at Middleborough and Kingston, so a commute to Boston is mostly a drive.

In 1989 Barnstable moved from selectmen and town meeting to a council and town manager system. It is one of thirteen Massachusetts municipalities with a city form of government that kept "the town of" in the name. In practice you deal with Town Hall at 367 Main Street in Hyannis, not a city hall.

sections.h2: Weather and the condition of the house
sections.html:
Snow averages about 30 inches a season from November through April, and February is usually the worst month, along with peak nor'easter activity. A buyer's inspector will look at the roof and the heating system first.

A cash buyer does not need those items repaired. If a storm has already damaged a roof or a deck, the house can still be sold as it stands.

Barnstable bills real estate tax in four quarterly payments each fiscal year. The first two bills are preliminary and fall due in early August and early November. The last two are actual bills, and for fiscal 2027 the dates are:

BillDue date
Third quarter (actual bill)February 1, 2027
Fourth quarter (actual bill)May 3, 2027

Actual bills are to be mailed by December 31, 2026. The Collector also bills motor vehicle and boat excise, sewer usage, and betterments for roads, water, sewer and septic. A betterment is a charge tied to the property, so mention any you know of to your closing attorney.

The Collector's page carries a municipal lien certificate request form. Ask your closing attorney whether your sale needs one. The Tax Collections line is 508-862-4054.

If you think the assessment is too high, an abatement application goes to the assessors. In towns that bill quarterly the application is generally due February 1, and the Appellate Tax Board hears appeals after that. Keep paying your installments while the request is open.

Most houses on septic need an inspection before a sale. Under the state's Title 5 rules, a system generally has to be inspected within two years before the sale, or within six months after it if weather prevents an earlier inspection. Barnstable bills for sewer and for septic betterments, so some addresses are on sewer and some are not. Find out which applies to yours.

  • Only MassDEP approved inspectors can do the inspection, and the report goes on the state form within 30 days.
  • The buyer must receive a copy of the report.
  • A passing inspection is generally good for two years. It is good for three years if the system is pumped every year and the records are in the report.
  • A conditional pass covers items like a cracked tank or a broken pipe, but cesspools and soil absorption systems cannot be repaired under a conditional pass.
  • A failed system must be upgraded within two years unless the Board of Health agrees to another schedule.

Transfers between spouses, parents and children, or full siblings are exempt, as are some trust and estate planning transfers. Buyers can also sign a binding agreement with the Board of Health to upgrade or connect to sewer within two years.

Massachusetts charges a deed excise tax when a deed is recorded, and the statute sets a lower rate for Barnstable County than for the rest of the state: $1.50 for each $500 of consideration or fraction of it. Recording fees are set separately by the registry, so ask your closing attorney for the current figure.

Three items come up in nearly every Massachusetts sale of a one or two family home.

  • Smoke and carbon monoxide certificate. You need a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing your alarms meet the sale rules. Call as soon as you have a closing date, and expect a fee. Battery alarms older than ten years must be replaced with sealed ten year photoelectric alarms.
  • An attorney. Massachusetts treats real estate closings as legal work, so plan to hire one.
  • Title system. Most properties are recorded land filed at the Registry of Deeds. A smaller share is registered land with a Land Court certificate of title.

State rules also stop sellers of certain residential properties from conditioning an offer on a buyer waiving a home inspection.

Seven villages mean seven different settings, from harbor streets in Hyannis to the wooded interior near Wequaquet Lake. A house in Cotuit and a house in West Barnstable can have very different sewer, water and tax situations, so confirm the details with the Collector and the Board of Health instead of assuming.

If the house needs septic work, carries a betterment, or sat vacant through a Cape winter, a direct sale can spare you the repair bills and the wait for an inspector. Cash Home Buyers buys Barnstable houses as they are.

faqs.q: Is Barnstable a town or a city?
faqs.a: Both. It keeps the name Town of Barnstable but has run under a council and town manager charter since 1989.

faqs.q: How many villages are in Barnstable?
faqs.a: Seven are commonly listed: Barnstable, Centerville, Cotuit, Hyannis, Marstons Mills, Osterville and West Barnstable. They have no legal boundaries.

faqs.q: When is the next Barnstable property tax payment due?
faqs.a: For fiscal 2027 the remaining dates are February 1, 2027 for the third quarter and May 3, 2027 for the fourth. Check your actual bill, since the Collector sets the schedule each year.

faqs.q: Do I need a septic inspection to sell my Barnstable house?
faqs.a: Usually yes if the home has a septic system. Title 5 calls for an inspection within two years before the sale, or within six months after if weather blocks it, unless an exemption such as a family transfer applies.

faqs.q: What is the deed excise tax in Barnstable County?
faqs.a: The statute sets $1.50 for each $500 of the sale price or fraction of it in Barnstable County. Your closing attorney can give you the exact amount.
